evals.prompt: Use the examples skill. I have a new feature request 'Two-factor authentication' to add to TaskFlow. Create it with acceptance criteria, estimate 5 points, label it type/feature + area/auth, and drop it into the current cycle 'Sprint 15'. Show me the exact MCP tool calls and name the reference file of the examples skill that gives the parameter formats. If you can't run it here, show me the exact calls you would make, in order, and what they return.
evals.expected_output: Concrete calls in order: project(action=list), label(action=list), cycle(action=list, status=current), workitem(action=create) with point and labels, cycle(action=manage_workitems) with add_ids, read back with list_workitems.
expectations: The answer says to resolve the label names to ids with label(action=list, project_id)
The answer says to create the item with workitem(action=create, ..., point=5, labels=[<label uuids>])
The answer says to find the cycle with cycle(action=list, project_id, status=current)
The answer adds the item with cycle(action=manage_workitems, project_id, cycle_id, add_ids=[<work item id>])
The answer says to read the cycle content back with cycle(action=list_workitems)
The answer names tool-patterns.md as the reference for the exact parameter formats

evals.prompt: Use the examples skill. Walk me through the full sprint lifecycle from planning to close in Plane. Read the sprint-lifecycle scenario reference and show me the tool calls at each phase. If you can't run it here, show me the exact calls you would make, in order, and what they return. Keep it brief: no preamble, the key points and calls first, about 15 lines in all.
evals.expected_output: The Monday-to-Friday scenario of sprint-lifecycle.md with its concrete calls: capacity, planning, standup, blocker, close and retro.
expectations: The answer puts the sprint capacity at about 15 points
The answer says to add the planned items to the sprint with cycle(action=manage_workitems, add_ids=[...])
The answer says to get the standup state totals with workitem(action=count, pql='cycle = "<id>"', group_by=state__group)
The answer says to record the blocker with workitem_relation(action=create, relation_type=blocked_by)
The answer says to close the sprint with cycle(action=complete) before cycle(action=archive)
The answer says to publish the retro notes with page(action=create)
